subject: Request: Detailed subprocessor routing, encryption proof, and export map
messages:
From: Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@greenbank.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: sec-team@greenbank.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request for detailed subprocessor routing + encryption evidence

Hi Laura / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. As we progress our DPA review I need a slightly more granular set of artifacts than what was in the standard subprocessor roster. Specifically GreenBank's procurement/security teams are asking for:  

- A data-export map that shows where customer data may egress to subprocessors (per service/component).  
- Encryption attestation for transit and at-rest for any third party that sees cleartext customer data.  
- Confirmation of S3/region residency for any storage providers that receive logs/exports.  

Can you provide those items (preferably consolidated into a single ZIP) and a short note describing any temporary/transient subprocessors (e.g., third-party support/maintenance vendors) and whether they can access EU/US production data? We have an internal deadline to close the DPA checklist by 2026-11-27.

If you'd prefer, send what you can now and we can follow up for details. Appreciate it.

Best,
Nisha Patel
Counsel, Vendor Risk — GreenBank

Attachment: (none)

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800

Hi Nisha — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick plan:  

1) Ben will pull together a combined dataflow diagram and a CSV of storage regions.
2) Irene will export the latest encryption attestation (we'll redact key material) and include our kms/HSM scope.
3) Kimberly will confirm which temporary/third-party vendors are used for on-call/maintenance and whether they have production access.

We'll deliver an initial package by EOD Monday 2026-11-23 and follow up with any outstanding items. If GreenBank needs any specific format for the attestation (signed letter, company header), tell us and we will accommodate.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security and Privacy
Redwood Inference

Laura / Kimberly —

Attached: greenbank_dataflow_diag.pdf (diagram with per-service arrows and subprocessors), s3_region_list.csv (rows: component, provider, bucket, aws-region). Notes:  

- Dataflow diagram includes labels for logs, KV cache snapshots, and long-term storage. Where logs are forwarded to third-party observability vendors we mark whether the data is redacted prior to export.

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@greenbank.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for detailed subprocessor routing + encryption evidence

Hi Nisha — following up with the encryption proof. Attached is a redacted encryption attestation that covers: TLS termination points, KMS providers, HSM scope, and encryption-in-use posture for cached model keys. We redacted key identifiers and internal IPs for security.

Short summary:  
- All customer payloads are TLS 1.2+ in transit; internal RPCs between services are mTLS with cert rotation.
- At-rest: customer content stored in S3 is encrypted with AWS KMS (customer tenant keys rotated via Redwood KMS integrations).
- Observability exports to third parties are filtered; if unfiltered exports are required we apply an explicit DPA amendment and isolated bucket routing.

Attachment: encryption_attestation_redacted.pdf
From: Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@greenbank.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request for detailed subprocessor routing + encryption evidence

Thanks — this is helpful and moves us forward. A few quick follow-ups before we close the checklist:  

1) GreenBank prefers signed attestations on company letterhead for encryption statements. Can you provide an attestation signed by someone in Security or Legal?
2) For the two telemetry buckets flagged as potentially PHI, can you confirm if masking/redaction is applied at source or downstream? If downstream, we need the change control ticket or process note that documents retention/erasure.
3) DocuSign: we also need the latest subprocessor addendum signed as part of our procurement flow. If you can route the envelope (HubSpot deal 78219 -> DocuSign) to me, Kim can sign and I will countersign.

If you can get the signed attestation and the masking confirmation by EOD Thursday 2026-11-26 we should be able to close. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best regards,
Nisha
Counsel, Vendor Risk — GreenBank
